title: River & Relay / Band 3: river arrival -> relay pickets -> officer -> relay captain -> captive -> Old Mill Crossing restored
_comment: Transcribed from docs/acceptance/GATE_F_MASTER_PROTOCOL.md section B (span), section D (RT-08, RT-09), section E.1 (CB-04's band 3 fights: relay ladder + relay_captain), section E.5 (objectives `defeat_the_relay_captain`, `rescue_the_captive`, `disable_the_relay`, `restore_the_mill_crossing`), section G (GF-10-RELAY-01/02/03, GF-21-WEATHER-03, GF-14-COMBAT-04c) and section H (0.1 Hz plus the band handoff window).
_comment_objective_order: objectives.json's main chain runs defeat_the_relay_captain (18/27), rescue_the_captive (19/27), disable_the_relay (20/27), restore_the_mill_crossing (21/27). Section B's span for S07 names the captain, the captive and the crossing and does not name disable_the_relay; it is transcribed in the chain's own order because the chain is what the quest log tracks.
_comment_evidence_lane: §H/§G evidence split, owner decision 2026-08-27, recorded in docs/acceptance/GATE_F_MASTER_PROTOCOL.md §H.1. This is the LOGIC lane: the journey run headless for mechanics, telemetry and step verdicts at 6.1 ms/frame against 12,721 ms for a rendered frame on the Gate F container. It takes no prescribed frame; the §G ids its steps would have taken are DELEGATED to S07C, which declares each of them in its "owes" list. The harness refuses to start this segment if S07C does not exist, does not declare evidence_lane=capture, or does not accept every id handed to it -- a delegation nobody accepted is a debt that has quietly stopped existing, which is the same shape as the 9,231 file:null PASSes CD-1 was written for. Whether the debt was actually PAID is a question about the whole run directory and is answered by tools/gate_f/run_inventory.py, not here.
_comment_record_hz_split: AMENDED for the §H/§G evidence split. record_hz is forced to 0 on a logic lane by the harness regardless of what this file says, because §H's continuous record is the thing the split removes: the recorder's cadence is counted in PLAY seconds now, but under a 12.7 s rendered frame even a 0.1 Hz record fires on every rendered frame, and the eighteen segments' 4,607,802 physics frames are ~8,283 hours. The obligation is not dropped -- §H's prescribed frames move to S07C, which may run BOUNDED record windows around a named state.

steps.title: how this segment is entered

args.text: Section B: this segment's entry save is `S06-exit`. The three steps below are the handoff's own mechanics: the live save directory is emptied first so the title's Load list has exactly one non-empty slot and auto-focuses it (`title_screen.gd` focuses the FIRST non-empty slot), then slot 4 is seeded from the run directory, then the load is driven through the production title-screen Load path by synthetic input. Section B names the seed and the Load path; the wipe is not named there and is recorded here as an added mechanical step, needed because an autosave left in slot 0 would take the auto-focus and the segment would load the wrong state.

steps.title: Section H band-handoff windows in this segment

args.text: Section H: 'Mandatory for the highest-risk segments: ... every band handoff +/-60 s (region transitions)'. The pairs in this segment raise the background recorder from the 0.1 Hz journey baseline to 0.5 Hz across each band boundary this segment crosses, and `record_stop` returns to the baseline rather than switching the recorder off, so the record stays continuous either side. AMBIGUITY RECORDED: +/-60 s cannot be sized exactly from a step script. A `move_to` leg's duration is not known before the run and a leg cannot be split, so each window is placed to contain the crossing plus as much of its approach and its settle as the surrounding steps allow -- erring long, because the schema's own measurement makes a 0.5 Hz window affordable as a window (1.05 ms/frame for its length) while a window that missed the transition would cost the evidence.

This fight and the two before it were split into shorter combat_quick blocks with a party_cycle between each (was one 38-tap block then one swap): the third run's own telemetry showed a fresh but solo ally (Pipwing, undamaged at 120hp) taking hits every ~0.65s and fainting before the ORIGINAL single mid-fight swap (38 taps in) ever fired, losing the fight to Vance's three-creature team with two more full party members never touched. steps.observation: GATE-D3-DECK, KNOWN LIMIT, not chased further. `disable_the_relay` is NOT part of section B's own S07 span (river arrival -> relay pickets -> officer -> relay captain -> captive -> Old Mill Crossing restored); it is objective 20/27 in the full chain and this segment's own S07-69 note already records that the protocol gives no site for it. Three straight attempts (a flat walk, a move_to_entity('Console'), then a four-waypoint ramp/gantry/pad chain -- see this run directory's own S07-superseded-6/7/8) all closed the horizontal gap to the Console node but stayed 4.7-4.9m short vertically: the console sits on a raised pad (`deck_y: 10.0`) reached by a real ramp, and `tests/smoke_relay_station.gd` (independently run and PASSING on this same SHA) proves the ramp itself works -- 'walked up the ramp... reached y=9.98 against a deck top of y=10.00' -- but ALSO proves approaching it from the wrong angle legitimately does not climb ('walked at the pad's flank from the yard; reached y=5.22'), which is exactly what this segment's own general-purpose, wall-following move_to/move_to_entity kept doing despite increasingly precise waypoints. This is a harness-navigator precision limit on one narrow ramp, not a Band3 game defect -- verified, not assumed. Reverted to the flat ground-level walk so this segment does not strand the player on the ramp/pad and block the in-scope Old Mill Crossing walk after it (S07-superseded-9's own S07-76 failed as exactly that knock-on). The console interact below is expected to refuse (relay_disabled will not be set) until a future pass gives this its own precision-walked waypoint chain or a dedicated capture-lane probe.

steps.observation: GATE-D3-CHANNEL. Section D's own (-152,4203) is the crossing's `channel.centre` (terrain_playground.json) -- the middle of the UNBUILT GAP, not a place to stand before the Gear restores the span. The previous target sent the walker straight at the void: it closed 3232m in the first 31492 frames and then spent the rest of its whole budget lodged 8.2m short, repeatedly falling in and getting returned to the road by severed_spokes.gd's carve failsafe (the earlier run's own log: 20+ 'player went over the edge... back to the road' lines at (-152,-7,4198)), because `close_enough: 4.0` against the centre demands standing inside the channel itself (half_length 6.0, so the gap alone runs 4197-4209). Retargeted at `gated_crossing.gd::near_point(7.4)` -- `centre - across*7.4` with `across=(0,1)` (derived here from the same `axis_deg: 0` / `_road_start()` rule the script itself uses, not eyeballed) -- which is also where `mill_crossing.gd`'s own Interactable prompt actually stands (`gate_offset: 7.4` in the same crossing's `bridge` block): (-152, 4195.6). It is 0.6m from where the walker organically stalled, so the earlier run had already effectively arrived and was failing only because the target it was still chasing was unreachable by construction.

steps.observation: RIG-14: opened via the map shortcut rather than a bare game_menu press. The pause shell REOPENS ON THE LAST TAB USED, so a fixed press count from an assumed backpack start lands on the wrong tab in any segment that opens the menu more than once -- this segment's own Section E.5 map-navigation notes leave the shell on `menu_map`, so the bare `open_menu` + `times: 5` this step used before landed on `menu_backpack` (5 presses from map wraps past save and back around to backpack), the Save button was never actually focused, and `save_out` then copied out whatever was already seeded in slot 4 under this segment's own name -- the exact mechanism RIG-10 named without yet fixing. `map` is one of only two tabs with a shortcut in data/config/menu.json, so it is the only deterministic starting point available. Matches S03/S06/S08's own working save steps.
